date_coverage_derivable_without_opening_.caution: All of the above is publisher-stated metadata. None of it has been verified against the scans, and it must not be treated as measured data.

provenance_note_on_wow_folder.publisher_statement: Both documentation files state that the Wow! artifact is owned and was scanned by the Ohio History Connection (also written as Ohio Historical Connection), and that its imaging configuration differs from the rest of the archive.
provenance_note_on_wow_folder.consequence_for_D1: The Wow! pages and the comparison population were produced by different imaging pipelines. Any property compared across them may be an artefact of digitisation rather than of the original record. This is the D1 analogue of the WOW v1 finding that a correct number can still be an invalid model input if its semantic type is wrong.

exposure_events.what_was_exposed: The page carries the publisher's own descriptions of features seen in the 1420 MHz continuum strip chart covering roughly one day following the Wow! event, at declination -27d 00m, from 16 August 1977 06h20m LMST to 17 August 1977 07h40m LMST. It names LMST times at which the galactic plane and several point sources appear, and mentions a noise-tube firing of unusual duration.
exposure_events.why_this_matters: This is content-derived description of the temporal region a future D2 comparison will concern, and it was read before the D2 amendment exists. It is prior published description, not our observation.
exposure_events.handling_rule: These statements are recorded as PRIOR PUBLISHED DESCRIPTION. They may not be presented as v2 findings, and any overlapping v2 candidate must cite this page in the novelty check. The D2 region must not be drawn to include or exclude these features on the basis of having read them.

exposure_events.what_was_exposed: Folder-level condition notes, greyscale and scan-quality remarks, the wow-folder boundary times and serial numbers, the stated thirty-page and five-page gaps, and an explicit open question by M. Abel dated 29 December 2017: whether the 3 AM run termination preceding the Wow! pages is unusual compared with other runs.
exposure_events.why_this_matters: The publisher has already posed, in public, a comparison question of the same shape as D1, and has already documented the gap structure around the Wow! pages. Neither can be claimed as a v2 discovery.
exposure_events.handling_rule: Recorded as PRIOR STATED QUESTION and PRIOR STATED STRUCTURE. A v2 candidate touching run-termination timing or the surrounding page gaps must cite this note in the novelty check and can at most contribute an answer, never the question.

exposure_events.what_was_exposed: Per-folder anomaly notes including mis-filed 1978 records, unit and column changes, printer failures, a stray frame, folders with poor legibility, and item-level remarks such as a note that folder 025 page 005 shows an interesting narrowband signal and that page 013-387 is marked as 14 August 1977 continued while the date has rolled to 15 August 1977.
exposure_events.why_this_matters: These are content-level observations about specific pages, read before any archive content was opened by us. Some of them concern exactly the kind of morphology and record-keeping anomaly D3 asks about.
exposure_events.handling_rule: Recorded as PRIOR PUBLISHED OBSERVATION. Any v2 candidate overlapping these notes must cite them in the novelty check. They may be used as structural context for planning access, never as a v2 finding.

unresolved_access_gaps.gap: scans/bin/, scans/jpg/ and scans/old/ were not retrieved. Their contents, counts and relationship to the png and cr2 trees are unknown.
The scans-level DIGESTS file and the per-folder SHA1SUM files were listed but not downloaded, so no published checksum has been verified.
Twelve numbered folders (073-078 and 151-156) are absent from both online trees while the README states 167 folders. Reason unknown.

Per-folder file counts and date coverage are known only for folder.wow. For all other folders the mapping from folder number to observing dates is unestablished, so the comparison population for D1 cannot yet be enumerated.

Whether the png and cr2 trees overlap in coverage, and whether either is a subset of the other, is not established. The numbered folder ranges are disjoint between the two trees, which suggests partition rather than duplication, but this is inference from names only.
The relationship between argus.naapo.org and naapo.org, and whether either mirrors the other, is not established.

The controller previously reported that the archive directory timed out. In this pass all listed retrievals succeeded. Whether availability is intermittent is not established, so no assumption of stable access is warranted.

No licence or reuse terms for the archive were located. The Wow! folder is stated to be owned by the Ohio History Connection. Rights for redistribution or derived publication are UNRESOLVED and must be settled before any scan is republished.

what_this_record_does_not_establish: It does not establish what the scans contain, whether any event other than the Wow! event is present anywhere in the archive, or whether the archive can answer D1, D2 or D3. Those remain open and are addressed only after the D2 amendment is sealed.
